A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 33-page paper, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical manuscript content apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp; PDF metadata also differs.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix G report original federated Q-learning simulations on randomly generated maze environments, including convergence curves, stepsize comparisons, and synchronization-period analyses.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix G retain the same original maze simulations and their reported outcomes, including five-run means and standard-deviation shading.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains identical synchronous local Q-learning updates and averaging every E iterations. The two-phase stepsize strategy discussed in Section 6 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same randomly generated 5×5 maze environments under homogeneous and heterogeneous conditions. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same constant, time-decaying, and two-phase stepsize strategies participate in the corresponding experiments. Table 1 remains an unchanged literature comparison rather than an additional empirical baseline evaluation.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix G retain identical settings, including 20 agents, discount factor 0.99, zero initialization, the stated 20,000-iteration horizon, infinity-norm error, and the same stepsize, synchronization-period, and tolerance settings.

E4.justification: The stepsize and synchronization-period sensitivity analyses, homogeneous-versus-heterogeneous comparisons, two-phase training analyses, final-error-versus-T plot, and target-tolerance analyses in Figures 2–8 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent runs and display means with shading extending one standard deviation above and below them. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All reported numerical values and plotted results in Section 6 and Appendix G are identical. For example, both report final error 2.75327 for the two-phase strategy with first-phase stepsize 0.05 and transition iteration 5550.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Lemmas 1–5, Theorems 1–2, Corollaries 1–2, and proofs in Appendices A–F are unchanged, including the conditional speedup and convergence-slowdown bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about convergence, conditional linear speedup, fundamental slowdown with multiple local updates under heterogeneity, and the empirical two-phase phenomenon.

C2.justification: Both retain the same heterogeneity-based explanation of residual error, discussion of difficulties analyzing time-varying stepsizes in Section 5.3, and qualification that estimating the phase-transition time remains future work.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures are identical, including maze generation, Bernoulli(0.05) rewards, drift probability 0.1, and initialization. No code/data access information or experimental instructions change.

R1.justification: Section 2, Table 1, and the reference list are identical. Comparisons with prior federated Q-learning, TD, and SARSA research and the claimed novelty of the lower bound remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 20 September 2025 to v3 dated 14 May 2026, and PDF author/license metadata changes. Manuscript prose, the visible author block, terminology, and section and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1, Algorithm 1, Figures 1–8, captions, and page layouts are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–33 are identical; the first-page difference is confined to the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The main text and Appendices A–G retain identical theory, proofs, empirical evidence, uncertainty reporting, and limitations. The administrative stamp and metadata updates leave the paper's scientific support, clarity, and reproducibility unchanged.
